entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - The Grand Finale on Linux Persistence
entries.description: By the end of this series, you'll have a robust knowledge of both common and rare Linux persistence techniques; and you'll understand how to effectively engineer detections for common and advanced adversary capabilities.

entries.title: Emulating AWS S3 SSE-C Ransom for Threat Detection
entries.description: In this article, we’ll explore how threat actors leverage Amazon S3’s Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C) for ransom/extortion operations.

entries.title: You've Got Malware: FINALDRAFT Hides in Your Drafts
entries.description: During a recent investigation (REF7707), Elastic Security Labs discovered new malware targeting a foreign ministry. The malware includes a custom loader and backdoor with many features including using Microsoft’s Graph API for C2 communications.

entries.title: From South America to Southeast Asia: The Fragile Web of REF7707
entries.description: REF7707 targeted a South American foreign ministry using novel malware families. Inconsistent evasion tactics and operational security missteps exposed additional adversary-owned infrastructure.

entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - Approaching the Summit on Persistence Mechanisms
entries.description: Building on foundational concepts and techniques explored in the previous publications, this post discusses some creative and/or complex persistence mechanisms.
